sections.title: Confusion pairs
sections.blurb: Most lost marks come from this short list. Each row is the one sentence that separates them.
rows: Synchronous, automatic failover, NOT readable = availability. Asynchronous, readable, manual promotion = performance.
S3 + DynamoDB only, free, route-based, not reachable from on-prem. Everything else, an ENI, chargeable, reachable over DX/VPN.
Work queue, deleted after processing, no replay. Ordered retained log, replayable, many consumers.
Real time, shards, replay, many consumers. Near real time (60 s buffer), managed, one destination.
Data replicates, NO servers running. A scaled-down but fully running stack.
Optimises speed. Enforces jurisdiction regardless of speed.
Is it healthy / how busy. Who called which API.
The API call that changed it. The resulting configuration state over time.
Stateful, allow-only, references other SGs. Stateless, ordered, the only place you can DENY.
Keeps environments warm — kills cold starts. Caps the share of the account pool — limits blast radius.
ECS pulls the image and writes logs. Your code calls AWS services.
Any key, any time, own capacity. Same partition key, creation time only, shares capacity.
Physical server with visible sockets and cores — socket-based BYOL. Isolated hardware, no visibility or placement control.
Charged, rotates automatically. Free standard tier, no rotation.
HTTP only, caches, DNS name. Any TCP/UDP, no caching, two static anycast IPs, sub-minute failover.
A privileged user can override. Nobody, including root, can delete until retention expires.
A user directory issuing JWTs. Exchanges an identity for temporary AWS credentials.
Persistence, replication, Multi-AZ failover, data structures. Simple, multi-threaded, disposable.
Alerts on a threshold. Analyses and forecasts what happened.
Any family/Region plus Fargate and Lambda. One family in one Region, slightly cheaper.

sections.title: Numbers worth memorising
sections.blurb: Facts that turn a 50-50 guess into a certainty.
rows: SQS message size / retention / visibility timeout
256 KB / 1 min – 14 days (default 4) / default 30 s, max 12 h
1 RCU = one 4 KB strongly consistent read/s (or two eventually consistent). 1 WCU = one 1 KB write/s
5 TB max / multipart required above 5 GB, advised above 100 MB
IA 30 d · Glacier IR & Flexible 90 d · Deep Archive 180 d
Flexible: 1–5 min expedited, 3–5 h standard, 5–12 h bulk. Deep Archive: 12 h standard, 48 h bulk
Spread placement group instances per AZ

sections.title: Automatic disqualifiers
sections.blurb: If an option contains one of these, it is wrong — even when the rest of it sounds right.
rows: Access keys hard-coded in application code, environment variables, user data or an AMI
Session state stored on the instances behind a load balancer
Databases in public subnets, or a publicly readable S3 bucket used to solve an access problem
The root user for day-to-day work, or root access keys existing at all
A single NAT gateway serving private subnets in several Availability Zones
A single Availability Zone in an answer to a high-availability requirement
Building custom code where a managed service does the same job, in a 'least operational overhead' question
Read replicas offered as a high-availability solution, or Multi-AZ offered as a read-scaling solution
Scanning a DynamoDB table where a Query or a GSI would work
Transitioning objects to Standard-IA before 30 days
Attaching an ACM certificate to an EC2 instance, or a CloudFront certificate outside us-east-1

sections.title: Reading the qualifier
sections.blurb: Several options usually work. The qualifier is what picks between them — read it first and last.
rows: Serverless, Spot, colder storage tiers, gateway endpoints, scaling to zero
Managed over self-managed: Lambda over EC2, Fargate over EC2, Aurora over self-hosted, Firehose over a custom consumer
Least privilege, roles not keys, private subnets, encryption, VPC endpoints, no public access
Multi-AZ, automatic failover, more redundancy — cost is not the concern
DMS with ongoing replication, blue/green, read replica promotion
Lift-and-shift friendly: EFS rather than rewriting to S3, Amazon MQ rather than SQS, RDS rather than DynamoDB
Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose — the word 'near' is doing real work
Multi-AZ inside one Region. A second Region exceeds the requirement and violates a cost qualifier
Second Region, cross-Region replication, Route 53 failover or Global Accelerator
